title: ERCOT Nodal Protocols (current)
why: The rulebook. Section 2 definitions, 4 DAM, 6 Real-Time, 7 CRRs, 8 performance monitoring, 9 settlements. Read the sections for your target role.

title: ERCOT Market Training
why: Free courses: ERCOT market fundamentals, Settlements, Day-Ahead, CRR, LSE and Generation Resource operations.

title: ERCOT Market Information & Grid Conditions
why: Prices, load, fuel mix and the market reports index.

title: ERCOT Public API Explorer
why: Free API for prices, load and disclosure data; build your own analyses with it.

title: ERCOT Committees & Meetings (TAC, PRS, WMS, ROS, Board)
why: Where rule changes are debated before they happen. Skim agendas monthly to have an informed NPRR opinion.

title: ERCOT Market Notices
why: Subscribe for system changes, settlement notices and emergency communications.

title: ERCOT Resource Adequacy reports (CDR, MORA)
why: The capacity outlook and monthly risk assessment every analyst should be able to discuss.

title: Potomac Economics: ERCOT State of the Market reports
why: The single best document for an analyst: what happened in the market last year and the IMM's recommendations.

title: FERC/NERC February 2021 Cold Weather Report
why: The definitive account of Winter Storm Uri's causes.

title: Grid Status
why: Clean ERCOT dashboards and blog; the open-source gridstatus Python package pulls the data.

title: Modo Energy: ERCOT research
why: Strong on batteries, ancillary services and RTC+B effects.

title: Doug Lewin: Texas Energy & Power
why: Policy and market commentary newsletter and podcast.

title: PUCT: ERCOT market and rulemakings
why: Market design decisions, large-load rules and resource adequacy dockets.

title: Texas Legislature Online
why: Bill text for SB 6, HB 1500, HB 4492 and the other laws that shape the market.

title: EIA: Texas profile and electricity data
why: Generation mix, gas prices and consistent historical data.

title: gridstatus Python package
why: pip install gridstatus; pulls ERCOT SPPs, load and fuel mix in a few lines.

title: NOAA Climate Data Online
why: Weather history for load-forecasting projects.

title: Understanding Today's Electricity Business (Shively & Ferrare)
why: Readable overview of how the power business works.

title: Power System Economics (Steven Stoft)
why: The theory behind energy-only markets and scarcity pricing.

title: Energy Trading & Investing (Davis Edwards)
why: Forwards, options and the risk metrics desks use.
